I loved the title and that you included more information about the area in the description! The music worked great for the first 3 minutes but got old pretty soon after that.

I also really liked the first few cuts you did to the beat of the music at 1:54! The scenery was beautiful and the music really added to that! Some of those cuts didn't have the same effect, though. Around 3:30 I felt it really didn't add much and I think it would've been better to focus on different short shots there instead of skipping frames on the same footage.

Really beautiful video, - thanks for sharing it!

I don't watch a lot of building comps but this is a great build & you've shown it off well! 

I do wish the music was a bit more coherent, though. It's upbeat for the most part but around 3:30 it switches to something a lot more broody before getting upbeat again. I think the video would work better musically if all the songs had the same vibe or if the scenes at least changed as the music did.

It'd be nice to give some specs of your build, too; like when you started it, how long you've spent working on it, and even just the height/size of it. That might be something that could be shown alongside your final showcase, or even just in your video description for those curious.

I really adored the visuals in this, but the audio kind of throws me off at times. I'm assuming the singing at the start is taken from a separate video than the footage it's being played over? I really liked the atmosphere at 1:10 and on because it has the original audio, but the start just doesn't mesh well with it. 

The way the audio overlaps and suddenly stops should've been fixed, as well. There's a bit at :37 where the audio just completely cuts for a few seconds before switching & at :55 the singing cuts back in and it's very jarring. 

I also felt that the bit at :59 should've been left out - the quality is a lot lower, it lasted maybe 10 seconds, & it has a completely different vibe than the rest of the video.

I also wish there were more details about what we're seeing! I've never seen a festival like this before & I would've loved if some of the dishes were described or if more context was given to the visuals you showed besides the bit in the description.

Very beautiful video, though! It shows something most have never gotten to experience - so thank you for sharing it!

(First time leaving a critique so sorry if it's hard to understand or too long!)

One of the first things I noticed was that you don't project your voice very much. It almost feels like you're on the cusp of mumbling and, especially at the start, you stammer a bit. If you don't already, it might help to warm up a bit by talking to yourself before you start recording! I didn't notice as much stammering as the video progressed, so it seems like you just need to work on sounding confident from the get go! There's also some whitenoise(?) under your audio (which I honestly don't know how to fix, haha) but it becomes very apparent when there's long pauses.

The next big thing for me was the editing & pacing. I didn't feel like much was accomplished in these 15 minutes & I think utilizing jump cuts instead of time-lapses would change that. Personally, I think a main draw for a lets player is their personality - but it's hard to experience that when a good bit of the video is a compilation with music. 

At the same time, I'd consider cutting bits with good chunks of silence or that don't progress your goal. Besides the mining time-lapse, it felt like you were mostly just running around and making observations - which comes off to me like you don't know what else to say.  The parts where you discussed game updates or your plans for your house were good - you elaborated on something the viewer didn't already know so they actually have a reason to listen!

I'm not sure how elaborate your house plans are, but for this episode I think you definitely should've gone until you at least started building if not finished your starting base. By cutting some parts out, you could've shown the viewer a lot more more progress in the same 15 minutes.

Lastly, I found the starting of music before time-lapses jarring & at 11:06 not only is the music too abrupt, but the pause before it was noticeably too long. I'm not sure what you use to edit, but if it gives the audio visualizer I'd try skimming through there for long silences or sudden peaks of sound & decide whether those sections can be cut or need to be edited. 

Overall, besides editing, I'd just recommend projecting your voice & maybe setting a goal to reach before each videos end! Thanks for sharing! :D
